title: Reversal of Paid Vision Services — Vision Plans Claims Guideline
content:
**When a paid service is reversed (Vision Plans).** A paid vision service is reversed in three cases:
- it duplicates a service already paid for the same person, kind and date of service;
- it was paid for a date of service on which coverage was not in force, including after a lapse back-dated to the paid-through date; or
- the provider reports a billing error.

**What a reversal does.** A reversal references the service it reverses and carries the original plan payment. The amount is recovered from the payee, and the frequency the service had used is restored. Each service can be reversed once.

**What a reversal is not.** A reversal is not used to change the member's choice of eyewear after it was ordered. Remakes for the same prescription are the provider's warranty matter and are not a new claim.

**One reversal per service.** Whether a service has already been reversed is read from the claim records. A reversal entry names the original service it reverses, and a service that already has a reversal entry naming it is not reversed again.

| Situation (hypothetical) | Reversed? |
|---|---|
| A frame paid twice for the same person on the same date of service | Yes — the duplicate |
| An exam paid for a date after the coverage termination date | Yes |
| The provider reports it billed the wrong lens type | Yes — billing error |
| The member prefers a different frame after the order | No — not a change of eyewear choice |
| A service that already carries a reversal | No — each service can be reversed once |
